dedupe_keys.name: australian mv lv distribution networks and demand profiles

description: This collection supplies four real Australian medium-voltage distribution networks with synthetic low-voltage extensions down to individual customers. The University of Melbourne team led by Nando Ochoa publishes anonymised AusNet Services inputs for two rural and two urban feeders in Victoria. The feeders use 22 kV medium voltage, with lower-voltage and single-wire earth-return variants where appropriate. Excel workbooks separate transformer and line parameters, while a ZIP archive contains NumPy residential demand profiles at thirty-minute resolution in kilowatts. The exact measurement calendar period is not stated in the README. Python notebooks and backend code support time-series power flow and network visualisation. Access is free under BSD 3-Clause, with separate included notices for OpenDSS and dss_python. A limitation is that the low-voltage circuits follow design principles and are not surveyed customer networks; demand is anonymised, which limits geographic and household linkage. Simulation uses include distributed-energy hosting capacity, voltage assessment and feeder loading. It relates to platform-opendss. The file tree and documentation were checked without downloading the workbooks or load archive, and no power-flow results were independently reproduced.
